_about: Chapter 6 (Travel): on the city bus, route 7. At the door: where to (twist: out of service, take the 12), the fare (twist: no change for a 500), sit anywhere, do you know where to get off; then a second set-up from the first seat: the ride, a stop called out, your stop, goodbye.

items.prompt: Ana, the bus driver, sits in the driver's seat about one third from the left, one hand on the big steering wheel, turned toward the open front door with a relaxed half smile as the learner steps up ("¡Buenas! ¿A dónde va?").

Change only her pose and expression: she shakes her head with an apologetic grimace, one palm raised, and points with her other thumb toward the back of the bus (she's out of service; the next bus is right behind her).
Change only her pose and expression: she holds out one open hand, palm up, toward the learner just above the small coin tray, a relaxed half smile (twelve pesos, cash only).

Change only her pose and expression: she holds up a large blank blue banknote (no numbers, no portrait, no words) between two fingers with a rueful smile, eyebrows raised; the small coin tray beside her holds only a few coins (no change for that: anything smaller?).
Change only her pose and expression: she gestures with an open hand down the aisle toward the worn seats, inviting the learner to sit anywhere, with a friendly smile.

Change only her pose and expression: she looks at the learner with eyebrows raised and a questioning half smile, one hand on the wheel and the other resting on the gear lever (do you know where to get off?).

The same city bus, now driving along a sunny street of painted one-story houses and palms, seen from the first passenger seat just behind the front door. Ana, the driver, sits about one third from the left with both hands on the big steering wheel, eyes on the road, her face in three-quarter view with a relaxed half smile (she'll say when to get off). Through the windshield: the street ahead, a speed bump, a few palms.

Change only her pose and expression: the bus has stopped at a stop beside the town's church, a lime-washed parroquia in white and ochre with a bell gable, seen through the windshield; she calls out over her shoulder toward the passengers, mouth open, one hand raised ("¡Iglesia! ¿Bajan?").

Change only her pose and expression: she glances back at the learner over her shoulder with eyebrows raised and points ahead through the windshield at a bus stop shelter coming up on the right side of the street (your stop: shall I stop?).
Change only her pose and expression: the bus has stopped at the curb by the stop shelter; she turns toward the learner with a cheerful wave and a warm smile ("¡Cuídese!").
